openQuestions.text: What is the merge collapse rule's real behavior on near-line pairs?
openQuestions.note: Zero near-line pairs exist in the tracked corpus; the class needs a manufactured set to reach a label gate.

openQuestions.text: Does the arbiter mean "same problem" or "same finding" when labeling?
openQuestions.note: 3 of 12 different labels are near-verbatim restatements confidently read as same; a second rater and a pre-registered question contract are required.

openQuestions.text: How many candidate pairs does a typical live fan-out run produce before commit?
openQuestions.note: The tracked corpus gives ~1.2 pairs per run; live pre-commit runs are invisible to the census and to the publication guard.

openQuestions.text: Does SAME_AT 0.4-0.45 generalize beyond the 60 recorded pairs?
openQuestions.note: 0.4 scores 57/60 post-hoc with flat specificity; a held-out pre-registered batch is required.
reader=none named on every verdict line; the record names the synthesis step and the system-deep-loop owner as candidates only.

resolvedQuestions.answer: The verdict was driven by corpus geometry: a single cross-body class with zero near-line pairs, a merge baseline that is structurally constant on that class, a 48:12 label split, and a per-pair record of 44/48 sensitivity and 9/12 specificity.
Accuracy: symmetric tiebreak (+2) and SAME_AT 0.4 post-hoc (+4). Cost: decision-equivalent early stop removes 58 of 181 calls with an identical verdict.

The keep is frame-dependent: stop (margin) against constant-same and against a lexical tie. Four labeled pairs are oracle-undecidable, 8 of 12 different labels are trivial dimension pairs from one run, and 3 labels are contested by confident near-verbatim reads.

Highest payoff: the merge's own exact-id question and ruled-out streams; then claim-continuity semantic candidates (contract already exists), conditional-fanin agreement, and contradiction-supersession candidate generation.

Needs a named reader, a phase amendment, a byte-identical fallback, a pair-keyed cache/guard decision and a pair cap. T0 census now, T1 shadow next, T3 model-as-collapse stays dropped. Measured risk: 6.4% false-merge on declared-same calls.
